title: Finite ordinary exchange under quotient coefficient realization
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, and its canonical integral datum [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Let Y -> X -> S and Y -> T -> S be a chosen Cartesian square. At any positive quotient level n+1, let F_W be the canonical exact function-coefficient realization. For every unbounded quotient-module complex J on T, the ordinary ringed exchange sbcFiniteExchangeApp [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange] is isomorphic as an arrow to F_X applied to the fixed-scalar derived exchange [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] at F_T inverse(J). No smoothness, properness, boundedness, or constructibility is assumed. The operations are those of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; coefficient maps have the normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], and their adjunction comparisons are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction].

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; Modules on Sites Tag 0D6D, functoriality of pullback; coefficient-realization portion of sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change proof step 2

proof.text: Use the canonical associated-module realization at each corner. Restriction along constant scalar sections is its inverse. Its sheafification unit and counit identify the underlying additive sheaves and determine the equivalence, including the zero ring and the empty scheme.

Ordinary direct images on both presentations evaluate on the same base-changed object. The canonical coefficient map sends each constant residue to the same residue. Identity on these sections is linear and gives the direct-image comparison. Conjugate under the tensor-normalized adjunctions to obtain inverse-image comparison, then derive the comparisons. Exact realization and its inverse preserve K-injective resolutions. The resulting comparisons preserve units and counits by the adjunction mate identities.

For two composable maps, both direct-image pasting comparisons restrict sections along the canonical iterated fiber-product isomorphism. Equality on sections and conjugation imply the pullback composition comparisons agree. The finite coefficient square is exactly the square of these constant-section maps. Substitute the unit, square, and counit identities into sbcFiniteExchangeApp. The endpoint comparison isomorphisms then define an isomorphism of arrows to realization of the fixed-scalar derivedBaseChangeMap.

proof_origin.place: Canonical coefficient change applied to the unit-square-counit definition of exchange, Tags 07A7 and 0D6D

lean.statement:
theorem sbcFiniteExchange_coefficient_realization
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    {X S T Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : T ⟶ S} {h : Y ⟶ X} {e : Y ⟶ T}
    (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare h e f g) (n : ℕ)
    (J : DerivedCategory (pbcModules T
      ((pbcAdicRings T (pbcIntegralDatum l E)).obj (Opposite.op n)))) :
    Nonempty (Arrow.mk (sbcFiniteExchangeApp l E sq n J) ≅
      Arrow.mk ((pbcDerivedFunctionRealization X (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n).map
        ((ProEtale.derivedBaseChangeMap
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ProEtale.PbcQuotient (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n))
          sq.toCommSq.flip).app
            ((pbcDerivedFunctionRealization T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n).asEquivalence.inverse.obj
              J))))
